summary: Parameterised governed metric families for the metric router: typed slots in, deterministic SQL out (metric_families.py). Vocabulary: config/agere/metric_vocabulary.json.

metrics.name: Patients matching a governed population
metrics.internal_reason: Composes governed concept, lab, medication, visit and roster definitions; each atom cites its own value set.
metrics.summary: Distinct roster patients whose records satisfy every population atom: conditions from the concept library (concept_patient: ICD-10-CM, SNOMED CT and adopted labels), lab results by concept (canonical units; "latest" = the lowest value on the most recent dated result, cancelled results excluded), latest paired blood pressure, age/sex/coverage from the roster, medications by governed drug group (picked up = pharmacy dispense with status dispensed; any_record = list, orders, dispenses, pharmacy claims or history), visits by governed visit class, positive social-needs screens, appointment outcomes. Returns the count, the list, a percent with numerator atoms, or a table by roster group.

population.summary: Roster patients (synthetic); the population slot narrows it.

denominator.summary: With returns=percent: the patients matching the population atoms.

numerator.summary: With returns=percent: those who also match the numerator atoms.

population.description: Who is counted, as predicate atoms (role all = must match, any = at least one of the any-atoms, exclude = must not match). Omit for the whole roster.

numerator.description: returns=percent (or a grouped table) only: atoms the population patients must ALSO match to count in the numerator (e.g. a lab result, a medication pickup, a visit).

returns.description: count = how many patients; patient_set = who (a list); percent = share of the population matching numerator.

group_by.description: Break the patients out by a roster attribute (age_band = 0-17, 18-44, 45-64, 65+). Grouped answers are tables.

metrics.name: Encounter volume by governed visit class
metrics.internal_reason: Volume counts over the governed visit-class value sets (metric_vocabulary.json); utilization_per_1000 conventions.
metrics.summary: Distinct encounters (encounter versions de-duplicated by encounter_id) whose received type belongs to the chosen visit classes, dated (event_date) in the period; optionally distinct patients, or visits per 1,000 roster patients (the whole roster of each group is the denominator, visit or not). Grouped by month, quarter, half-year, year, facility or a roster attribute.

population.summary: Roster patients (synthetic); the population slot narrows it.

denominator.summary: None (count) unless the slots ask for a rate.

numerator.summary: Distinct encounters (encounter versions de-duplicated by encounter_id) whose received type belongs to the chosen visit classes, dated (event_date) in the period; optionally distinct patients, or visits per 1,000 roster patients (the whole roster of each group is the denominator, visit or not). Grouped by month, quarter, half-year, year, facility or a roster attribute.

period.description: Date window the metric counts. preset: all_time (default for any-time questions; undated records count), year (+year), ytd, trailing_months (+months, ending at the snapshot date inclusive), trailing_days (+days), before_days (+days: only records dated at least that many days before the snapshot), custom (+start, +end ISO dates).

measure.description: visits = distinct encounters; patients = distinct patients with one; per_1000_roster = visits x 1000 / roster patients.

group_by.description: facility = the organization where the visit happened; attributed_practice = the patient's assigned PCP practice.

population.description: Who is counted, as predicate atoms (role all = must match, any = at least one of the any-atoms, exclude = must not match). Omit for the whole roster.

metrics.name: Follow-up after an index visit
metrics.internal_reason: Follow-up windows follow definitions.json follow_up_after_ed conventions; the visit classes are governed value sets.
metrics.summary: Index encounters of the chosen classes dated in the period; an index visit is followed up when the same patient has a different encounter of the follow-up classes dated days_min..days_max days after the index date (visit date, or discharge date for stays). Returns the number or the percent of index visits followed up.

population.summary: Roster patients (synthetic); the population slot narrows it.

denominator.summary: None (count) unless the slots ask for a rate.

numerator.summary: Index encounters of the chosen classes dated in the period; an index visit is followed up when the same patient has a different encounter of the follow-up classes dated days_min..days_max days after the index date (visit date, or discharge date for stays). Returns the number or the percent of index visits followed up.

days_min.description: 0 = same day counts; 1 = from the next day.

fully_observed.description: Only index visits whose whole follow-up window ends by the snapshot date.

period.description: Date window the metric counts. preset: all_time (default for any-time questions; undated records count), year (+year), ytd, trailing_months (+months, ending at the snapshot date inclusive), trailing_days (+days), before_days (+days: only records dated at least that many days before the snapshot), custom (+start, +end ISO dates).

population.summary: Roster patients (synthetic); the population slot narrows it.

denominator.summary: None (count) unless the slots ask for a rate.

numerator.summary: Mean (or median) of end_time - start_time over completed stays of the chosen classes, in days or hours; the period applies to the admission or the discharge date.

metrics.name: Medical claim outcomes
metrics.internal_reason: Revenue-cycle conventions (first-pass denial, overturn, net of reversals) encoded on the claim grain.
metrics.summary: One row per medical claim (adjudication versions settled in the claim table): first-pass status, ever denied, denied then paid, net payer paid (every adjudication delta, reversals net out), billed/allowed, and days from service to first submission, first adjudication and first payer cash. The period applies to the service date, or the benefit year.

The period applies to the service date, or the benefit year.

metrics.summary: Per received stream: rows, rows with no event date, percent undated, mean arrival lag (available_date - event_date) and rows arriving more than N days after the event; encounters can be counted once per encounter_id (first arrival, earliest date).

lag_op.description: gt = more than lag_days; ge = lag_days or more.
